reasoning: Residues mod 7 of 1..100: since 100 = 14*7 + 2, residues 1 and 2 each occur 15 times, residues 0,3,4,5,6 each occur 14 times. Two distinct elements sum to a multiple of 7 iff their residues are (0,0), (1,6), (2,5), or (3,4). So a valid subset contains at most 1 element with residue 0, and for each complementary pair can only use one residue class of the pair, giving at most max(15,14)+max(15,14)+max(14,14)+1 = 15+15+14+1 = 45. Construction achieving 45: all n in {1..100} with n ≡ 1 (mod 7) — {1,8,...,99}, 15 numbers; all n ≡ 2 (mod 7) — {2,9,...,100}, 15 numbers; all n ≡ 3 (mod 7) — {3,10,...,94}, 14 numbers; plus the single number 7. Any two distinct elements have residue sum in {2,3,4,5,6,1,2,3} mod 7 or (with 7) residue 1,2,3, never 0. Total 45.
